To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proton-pumping pyridine nucleoide transhydrogenase from Escherichia colt has a transmembrane proton pathway that is lined by betaAsn222, betaHis91, and betaGlu124.

the pyridine transhydrogenase has a proton translocation pathway through domain II of the membrane that is accessible from the cytosol and that betaGlu124 and betaAsn222 are important for proton translocation.

the proton-pumping pyridine nucleoside transhydrogenase from Escherichia Coli contains an aqueous cavity that runs from the cytoplasmic side of the membrane to the region of a key residue, betaHis91, in helix 9.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of proton transfer across the membrane domain of the transhydrogenase.
the identification of residues in domain II of the pyridinetide transhydrogenase that are involved in translocation of hydride and protons across the cytoplasmic membrane.
the elucidation of the mechanism of proton translocation in the pyridine transhydrogenase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transmembrane helical domain of the pyridinenucleotide transhydrogenases is composed of a series of transmembrane helicies with a number of residues in these helices involved in proton translocation and permeation.
the proton pathway across the membrane domain of pyridine nucleotides transhydrogenase involves the residues betaHis91, betaGlu124, and betaAsn222.
there is an aqueous cavity from the cytosol to the region of the betaHis91 residue in helix 9 of domain II of the transhydrogenase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proton translocation pathway through domain II of the enzyme is a water-filled pore that is lined with charged and polar amino acid residues.

the proton pathway in the pyridine transhydrogenase consists of a water-filled pore that extends from the periplasmic surface of the membrane through the membrane domain to a site near betaHis91 in helix 9.
the proton translocation pathway across domain II is composed of three components: (i) a proton-permeable channel, (ii) a proton-conducting pathway, (iii) a proton-translocating pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proton pathway across the membrane domain of the pyridinenucleotide transhydrogenases of E. coli and yeast is similar to the pathway of the proton pump of the F(0) domain of F(1)F(0)-ATPases.
the proton translocation pathway through the membrane domain of the enzyme is a water-filled channel.
the proton translocation pathway through domain II is a continuous aqueous cavity that extends from the cytosol to the region of the betaHis91/betaGlu124 residues.
